text: Reprogramming human somatic cells to pluripotency was first achieved with OCT4, SOX2, KLF4, and c-MYC. Subsequent work replaced original factors, but OCT4 had not been successfully substituted in human cells, unlike in mouse. Using transcriptome and bioinformatic analysis, researchers identified lineage-specifier factors able to replace OCT4 and SOX2 in reprogramming human fibroblasts. Results show OCT4 and SOX2 can be replaced simultaneously by alternative lineage specifiers, supporting a model in which counteracting lineage-specification networks underlie pluripotency induction. Separately, DNA methyltransferase and histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitors improve reprogramming efficiency; valproic acid (VPA), an HDAC inhibitor, boosts efficiency over 100-fold (using Oct4-GFP reporter) and enables efficient induction of pluripotent stem cells without the oncogene c-Myc.
